topic.subject: science
topic.title: Life processes
topic.scope: nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion in plants and animals, kidney and nephron

misconceptions.statement: Plants get their food from the soil through their roots.
misconceptions.why: Students observe plants growing in soil and assume soil is the source of mass.
misconceptions.fix: Plants make their own food (glucose) using sunlight, CO2, and water; soil only provides minerals and water.

probe.question: If a plant grows in a pot, why doesn't the weight of the soil decrease significantly?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the plant only takes a tiny bit of soil food.

misconceptions.root_belief: external source is the only source of food

misconceptions.statement: Respiration and breathing are the same process.
misconceptions.why: The terms are used interchangeably in everyday conversation.
misconceptions.fix: Breathing is the physical act of gas exchange, while respiration is the chemical breakdown of food to release energy inside cells.

probe.question: Does respiration occur in a person who is holding their breath?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because they are not breathing.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Plants only respire at night and photosynthesize during the day.
misconceptions.why: Students think photosynthesis replaces respiration in plants during the day.
misconceptions.fix: Respiration is a continuous process in all living cells, occurring both day and night to maintain life.

probe.question: When do plant cells use oxygen to break down glucose?
probe.wrong_answer: Only at night when there is no sun.

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause or time
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver's Children's Ideas in Science

misconceptions.statement: Arteries always carry oxygenated blood and veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
misconceptions.why: This is the general rule taught initially, ignoring the pulmonary circuit exceptions.
misconceptions.fix: Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it towards the heart; pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood.

probe.question: Which vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
probe.wrong_answer: Pulmonary vein, because it must be oxygenated.

misconceptions.statement: Excretion is the process of getting rid of undigested food (feces).
misconceptions.why: Both involve removing 'waste' from the body, leading to linguistic confusion.
misconceptions.fix: Excretion is the removal of metabolic nitrogenous wastes like urea; removing undigested food is called egestion.

probe.question: Is passing stool an example of excretion in the biological sense?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is waste leaving the body.

misconceptions.statement: The heart is responsible for creating or purifying the blood.
misconceptions.why: The heart's central role in circulation leads to over-attributing functions to it.
misconceptions.fix: The heart only pumps blood; blood cells are made in bone marrow and purified (oxygenated) in the lungs.

probe.question: What happens to blood when it enters the heart?
probe.wrong_answer: It gets cleaned and turned back into red blood.

misconceptions.root_belief: the most visible part does everything

misconceptions.statement: The kidney acts like a sieve that just lets small things fall through.
misconceptions.why: Simplified analogies of 'filtration' lead to a passive view of the organ.
misconceptions.fix: Kidneys use complex pressure-based filtration and active selective reabsorption to maintain balance.

probe.question: Why doesn't glucose normally appear in urine if it is a small molecule?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the kidney sieve holes are too small for glucose.

misconceptions.root_belief: complex processes work like simple mechanical tools

misconceptions.statement: Water moves up a tree because the roots push it up.
misconceptions.why: Students find it easier to imagine a push from the bottom than a pull from the top.
misconceptions.fix: While root pressure exists, the main force for tall trees is the transpiration pull caused by evaporation from leaves.

probe.question: How does water reach the top of a 100-meter tall redwood tree?
probe.wrong_answer: The roots pump the water with high pressure.

misconceptions.root_belief: movement requires a push from behind

misconceptions.statement: Energy is produced in the lungs during breathing.
misconceptions.why: Students associate the intake of oxygen directly with the immediate production of energy.
misconceptions.fix: Lungs only exchange gases; energy (ATP) is produced inside every individual cell during cellular respiration.

probe.question: Where exactly is the energy in your body generated?
probe.wrong_answer: In the lungs when we inhale oxygen.

misconceptions.root_belief: the organ is the only site of function

misconceptions.statement: The small intestine is smooth inside to let food slide easily.
misconceptions.why: Everyday experience with pipes suggests smooth surfaces are better for flow.
misconceptions.fix: The small intestine has millions of tiny finger-like projections called villi to increase surface area for absorption.

probe.question: What would happen if the inner lining of the small intestine was perfectly smooth?
probe.wrong_answer: Digestion would be faster because food moves quickly.

misconceptions.statement: Anaerobic respiration only happens in bacteria and yeast, not humans.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often emphasize yeast fermentation as the primary example.
misconceptions.fix: Human muscle cells undergo anaerobic respiration (producing lactic acid) during vigorous exercise when oxygen is low.

probe.question: Why do your muscles ache after a very fast sprint?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they ran out of air and stopped respiring.

misconceptions.root_belief: biological processes are exclusive to certain groups

misconceptions.statement: The body gets rid of all the liquid it filters in the kidney.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that once something is 'filtered' out of the blood, it is gone.
misconceptions.fix: Most of the initial filtrate (water, glucose, amino acids) is selectively reabsorbed back into the blood.

probe.question: If 180 liters are filtered by kidneys daily, why do we only pass 1-2 liters of urine?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the rest evaporates from the skin.
